name: rfid:hall switch below the standing spot
detail: top of the hall switch 6.8 mm below the standing surface, on the axis of the spot: its element lies 8.3 to 9.3 mm below the pole face of a magnet of a classic Tonie (Ø6 x 6 mm, set 1-2 mm into the foot). An ideal magnet on the axis gives 19 to 24 mT there; by the table of research/09 section 7 a magnet 8 mm off the axis still gives about 6 mT, and two magnets 20 mm apart with like poles down about 6.5 mT. The switch needs 4.8 mT at most. Not covered: two magnets with unlike poles down, which cancel on the axis; the reader's IRQ line is wired as the second way to wake
